correctness.rationale: In the frozen RESULT.md lines 5–22 the bracket map on Λ²sl₂ is invertible over any field of characteristic different from 2 (its determinant in the displayed bases is a signed power of 2). Thus the rank≤1 equation is the full minors ideal of the projected tautological map. On a rank-one chart a unit pivot makes both its kernel and image line bundles; the remaining mixed wedge equation identifies their lines in the two copies of the three-space. The lift modulo this line is a map ℓ→g/ℓ, giving the total space of the tangent bundle over P(g), as schemes. The boundary charts are obtained by inverting any nonzero vertical minor, without requiring the point to be rational. Elimination on such a chart uniquely solves c_2=−a_1, a_3=a_2b_2+b_1a_1, c_3=b_1c_1−a_1b_2; the residual ideal is exactly (a_1²+a_2c_1). Direct 2×2 commutator Gröbner reduction also checked this over Q (python3 /tmp/opencode/frozen_math_reproduction.py). Over every extension the hypersurface is integral with singular ideal (a_1,a_2,c_1) from its Jacobian and is Cohen–Macaulay and regular in codimension one; this and the smooth open give geometric normality. The boundary is in the closure of the integral open by the displayed one-parameter deformation, and the regular open plus integral charts ensure no extra or nonreduced components. The resolution map is regular via local Plücker wedges of τa+εb and εa: these are never zero on a fiber, glue projectively, and satisfy the bracket equations. The open τ≠0 recovers the tangent bundle; at infinity the map identifies with the incidence flag map (ℓ ⊂ plane) to Gr(2,g), as a scheme, giving P¹ fibers and the stated exceptional divisor. A rank-two vector bundle and the vertical Gr(2,3) give (Q²+Q+1)(Q²+1) independent of extension degree; the zeta exponents are its monomial coefficients. The symbolic finite check is limited to one rational coefficient chart; the supplied finite census was inspected, not run, and neither proves generality or finite-field counts in extensions.

value.rationale: The abelian-plane Grassmannian is a natural subalgebra moduli scheme in the first Takiff extension of sl₂. Identifying its exact singular ideal and explicit contraction, rather than only enumerating planes or giving the dense open, determines how the tangent-bundle moduli compactifies, with control under field extension. The arithmetic is a useful check and consequence, not the main novelty.
